short_description: 76 printable play cards for ages 1–5, sorted by age and energy. Each has what you need, a talk line and a safety line. PDF in Letter and A4.
long_description:
76 printable play cards for ages 1–5, in two age bands: 1–3 and 3–5. It is a PDF download in US Letter and A4.

When your child says “I’m bored,” pull a card and play. Most cards use things you already have: pots, socks, boxes and paper. 70 of the 76 cards need nothing to buy.

Each card has an age band and a starting age. It shows the energy level: calm, medium or wiggly. It lists what you need, prep time, mess and a rough play time. It gives short steps, one thing to say while you play, and a safety line. Every card says “With a grown-up.”

A two-page grown-up guide shows how to start in two minutes. It has three talk tips and a pantry list. The card index gives an easier way, a harder way and a 2-minute tired-grown-up way for every card.

You also get 14 blank cards, card backs, 20 box dividers, 12 jar labels, a Play Menu, weekly planners and a fridge certificate.

You get five PDFs: START HERE, color and low-ink, each in Letter and A4. In the color files you can type in the blank cards, labels, dividers, planners and certificate. You can type text and tick circles. You can’t change fonts, colors or pictures.

Every play follows our published safety rules. Digital file in English; nothing is shipped. Personal license for one household.

license_tiers.covers: One household: print and copy for your own home, including grandparents and sitters who care for your child. Sold on Etsy and our site. A gift passes this license to the family that receives it.

faq.a: 76 plays: 38 play cards for ages 1–3 and 38 for ages 3–5. Also a 2-page grown-up guide, a card index with an easier, harder and 2-minute version of every card, 14 blank cards, card backs, dividers, jar labels, a Play Menu, planners and a certificate.

About 15 minutes to print and cut every card with a paper trimmer, once. Each card shows its own prep: none, 2 minutes or 10 minutes. 70 of the 76 need nothing to buy. No time to cut? Read titles from the card index and let your child pick.

Instant download: nothing ships. On Etsy your files stay on your Purchases page; on our site the link is in your order email and on the re-download page. On a phone, use a web browser, not the shopping app, and save each PDF.
Pick one: US Letter or A4, color or low-ink. Every file has the same 36 pages. START HERE and the page guide on page 8 show what to print first.
The personal license ($6.50) covers your own household, including grandparents and sitters who care for your child. It is the only license offered right now.

faq.q: Can I give it as a gift?
faq.a: Yes. Print and cut the cards, put them in a jar with one of the 12 labels, and give the jar. Or forward the download to the family. The personal license then belongs to that family.

faq.q: Can a classroom, child-care center, library or PTA use it?
faq.a: Not yet. This pack is licensed for one household. Classroom, child-care, library and group licenses are not available yet.

Not yet: the text is in English. The guide says to talk, sign, sing and read in the language you know best, and every talk line works in any language. A Spanish edition would be made by a human translator.

faq.q: My child dislikes mess or loud noise.
faq.a: Skip those cards or use the easier version: a spoon instead of hands, a towel on the pot, watching first. Every card shows its mess level, and every child may pass.

faq.q: Does it work for children who sign, point or use a talking device?
faq.a: Yes. A sign, a point or a device tap counts as an answer. No card asks for eye contact, and Mirror Faces can be played side by side at a mirror.

Every play follows our published safety rules. Ages 1–3 cards use only things too big to fit through a toilet-paper tube, every card has its own safety line, and every card says “With a grown-up.” You know your child best: skip anything that doesn’t suit them.
No. These are everyday play ideas for families. Questions about your child’s development? Your child’s doctor is a good place to start.
Digital downloads follow the shop’s published refund policy, which is linked on every product page and at checkout. If a file won’t open or print, we fix it or send it again.

faq.q: Is there a printed deck or a book?
faq.a: Not yet. If a printed edition is made, we will say so here.
Ages 1 to 5, in two bands: 1–3 and 3–5. Every card also shows the age it usually starts from. Ages are a guide, never a deadline.

compliance_notes: Rule 1: no health, medical, therapy, developmental or outcome claims; the last page says the cards are parent education, not medical or developmental advice. No diagnosis words in the product, images, keywords or tags. Rule 2: no company, app or device is named; the fill-in instructions say 'a free PDF reader that supports fill-in forms' and downloads say 'use a web browser, not the shopping app'. Rule 4 child safety, audited card by card (all 186): every card has its own safety line; every card for under-5s is flagged 'With a grown-up'; every Ages 1–3 card and every seasonal card that includes age 1 uses only things too big to fit through a toilet-paper tube (fixed in this audit: palm-size crayons instead of chunky crayons, a wide brush, big spoons and big cups, no sticks on the toddler nature walk); older cards with small things (coins, dice, tape, seeds, dough, shakers) say to keep them from under-3s; no balloons; no cords, strings, ties or long scarves (cloth strips are short; bags are paper or cloth); every water card says grown-up within arm's reach; no whole grapes, nuts, popcorn, hard candy or marshmallows, and snack cards use thin, soft pieces (cheese cubes removed); grown-ups handle knives, stove, oven, glass and tools. Every cut piece is 1.5 in or larger (cards 2.5 × 3.5, small labels 2.3 × 1.6, dividers 2.4 × 3.95, round labels 3.4); cut sheets print 'Grown-up keeps the pieces'; hook-and-loop dots are for ages 3+ with 'Check dots before each play; remove any that lift' and a no-dots route for under-3s. Rule 5: only the WHO 2019 under-5 guidelines are cited. Rule 6: talk tips in plain words, no program names. Rule 7 and logo: original titles, art and layout; supplied logo files only, one-color white on grass, plum, sky and tomato, reverse on ink, primary on sun. Customer-voice rules: color + low-ink files in Letter and A4, plain PDFs under 15 MB, START HERE first, no URL or QR in Etsy files, version footer on every page, prep budget on page 1 and in the listing, prep/mess/time icons and starting age on every card, easier/harder and 2-minute versions for every card, 90% 'Nothing to buy', corner flags, no quiz or trivia cards (Family Trivia replaced by Clue Trail), 2-page grown-up guide with 'most children love 2–3 of these', home-language line, pediatrician line on the stage page, blank + pre-filled + fillable planners, labels and dividers. Small text is ink on white chips or tints (no white small text on tomato, sky or grass). Honest pricing: no anchor or 'was' price. AI-assisted content is never described as human-made. Customer panel (September 28, 2026, see panel.md): 'Sock Puppet Hello' renamed 'Sock Friend Hello' (BRAND.md logo section keeps 'sock puppet' out of marks); talk lines that asked a toddler to say a word now model it ('More bubbles? More!', 'Again? Again!', 'Quack, quack! Your turn, duck.'); Mirror Faces can be played side by side at a mirror; 5–12 cards that a child reads no longer say 'your child'; the rain gauge is plastic, not glass; the license names grandparents and sitters; classroom, center, library and group licenses are HELD (ops/QUEUE.md), so the PDFs say they are not available yet; English-only is stated in format, language and faq.
